title: Implicit Quarantine & Checksummed Snapshot Rehydrate Drill
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Goal: Validate an active-passive DR path that (1) applies an implicit quarantine to a degraded passive region without manual gating, (2) rehydrates service state from a checksummed snapshot, and (3) verifies correctness with an end-to-end canary and SLO regression guardrails. This ticket builds automation, verification tooling, and the runbook for a scheduled rehearsal that minimizes blast radius and enables rapid rollback.

Why: Current drills require manual operator fencing and have flaky snapshot verification. We need a repeatable mechanism so on-call or automation can isolate a passive region when divergence or partial corruption is detected, restore from a verified snapshot, and safely reintroduce it without impacting global SLOs.

Scope / Non-goals: Includes KV snapshot export/import, checksum tooling, automatic implicit quarantine trigger (based on divergence heuristics), canary traffic rehydration, and CIRCUIT-BREAKER tuning for staged traffic reintroduction. Does NOT include full control-plane VPC reconfiguration or long-term data migration between customers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Automation can run a scheduled drill that:
  * injects controlled divergence into passive region (small write fanout),
  * triggers implicit quarantine within operator-defined thresholds,
  * snapshots and rehydrates passive region from S3-backed snapshot with per-shard checksums,
  * runs a deterministic canary suite that validates read-after-write across 95th percentile latency SLOs,
  * records checksum parity across shards and emits a pass/fail signal to console and PagerDuty.
- Rollback path documented and automatable within 10 minutes of failure.
- Metrics dashboard with delta from baseline SLOs (error rate, p95 latency, token cost) produced automatically.

High-level plan:
1) Implement checksum metadata in snapshot manifest and fast verifier (Go): GH PR draft at https://github.com/redwood-inference/infer-runner/pull/682.
2) Extend orchestration to support implicit quarantine rule: policy accepts divergence score, circuit-fence TTL, and severity tier.
3) Add staged rehydrate job that performs snapshot import with integrity checks and KV version reconciliation.
4) Build canary harness (node/python) that exercises read/write patterns representative of production latency sensitive paths.
5) Create a runbook and a toggle in Console to kick off the drill and observe health panels.
6) Run a smoke rehearsal in test lab, then an internal tabletop, then a low-risk prod rehearsal during maintenance window.

Metrics to capture:
- Pre/post drill: p95 latency, error rate, requests/sec, tokens/sec.
- Time to quarantine decision, time to complete rehydrate, time to reenable region.
- Snapshot checksum mismatch rate and number of corrected shard patches.
- Canary success ratio and SLO delta.

Rollback and safety controls:
- Circuit-breaker policy will short-circuit traffic to passive region if canary failure > 5% in 3m.
- Global routing fallback to primary region with gradual ramp to avoid head-of-line surges.
- Snapshot imports run into isolated staging units by default; manual promotion required to serve unless canary passes.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELIABILITY/Implicit+Quarantine+DR+Drill
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infer-runner/pull/682 (snapshot verifier)
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/490 (implicit quarantine policies)
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/DR/implicit-quarantine-drill

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Checksum verifier performance may add snapshot restore time. Mitigation: verify only high-risk shards by default and support full-verify as opt-in.
- Risk: Partial import leaves passive region inconsistent. Mitigation: staging import + atomic promote controlled by canary pass.
- Risk: Circuit-breaker thresholds too sensitive causing unnecessary failover. Mitigation: run parameter sweep in test lab and set canary annealing window.
